summary: Remote-controlled agent grants shell, filesystem, and package-install control via WebSocket
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent is a long-running Node.js agent that opens an outbound WebSocket to a configurable SERVER_URL and dispatches server-sent messages to privileged local handlers. Received `terminal_input` frames are written directly into a spawned PTY (bash/powershell/pwsh) via `term.pty.write(msg.data)`, giving the remote endpoint full interactive shell control of the host running the agent. The same message router handles `terminal_create`, `write_file`, `delete_files`, `git_push`, and `upgrade_agent`; the upgrade handler spawns a detached bash/wscript script that runs `npm install "$PKG"@latest`, allowing the remote party to swap in arbitrary packages. `service/linux.js` also installs the agent into user PATH via `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` entries, and bundles msal-browser as part of the auth flow. The default SERVER_URL is loopback, but the configuration accepts any host, and once the agent is pointed at (or coerced to) a non-local server, that server has arbitrary code execution, filesystem mutation, git push using the host's credentials, and self-updating package install on the machine running the agent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
